state_specific_warning: Texas housing procedure is document- and fact-specific. Statewide rules provide the baseline, but lease terms, subsidized-housing rules, bankruptcy, military-service status, disability law, loan type, and approved local court rules or standing orders can change the path.

local_variation.statewide_rule: Texas statewide statutes and Supreme Court rules supply the baseline. Local rules, forms, and standing orders may govern local practice but may not conflict with controlling law or statewide rules.

notice_to_vacate.label: NOTICE TO VACATE
notice_to_vacate.court: Texas Justice Court after suit is filed

immediate_clock.label: Pre-suit notice period
exceptions: written lease or agreement may provide a different period
reason for possession and statutory exceptions can change the rule
immediate_clock.display: Do not assume every Texas notice is exactly three days. Read §24.005 together with the lease and the notice.

do_now: Read the notice and lease together. Identify the stated reason, move-out date, delivery method, and whether the landlord demands rent, possession, or both.
Save the notice, envelope or posting photo, lease, rent ledger, payment proof, messages, accommodation requests, and military-service documents if relevant.
notice_to_vacate.next_stage: If suit is filed, the next controlling document is the Justice Court citation and trial setting.

court_citation.label: COURT CITATION
court_citation.optional_filing: Written answer may be filed on or before the trial date under Rule 510.11; a general denial is sufficient.

immediate_clock.label: Trial / appearance
exceptions: a separately served summary-disposition motion can create a different response period
immediate_clock.display: A written answer is not required in an ordinary Texas eviction case. Do not miss the trial date printed in the citation.

do_now: Confirm the court, cause number, trial date and time, service date, plaintiff, property address, and claims.
Bring the lease, notices, payment proof, communications, photos, accommodation requests, military-status evidence if relevant, and witnesses or documents supporting defenses.

judgment.label: JUDGMENT
judgment.required_filing: To perfect an appeal, use an appeal bond, cash deposit, or Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs as Rule 510 permits.

immediate_clock.label: Eviction appeal
exceptions: Rule 510 has special time-computation and filing rules; do not substitute ordinary civil counting or assume mailing is timely
immediate_clock.display: Texas eviction appeals generally must be perfected within 5 days after the judgment is signed.

do_now: Get the signed judgment and record the signing date—not merely the date you received a copy.
If considering appeal, act immediately and read current Rule 510.19 and the court instructions on bond, cash deposit, Statement of Inability, rent registry, and county-court transfer.
judgment.stay_possession_consequence: A perfected appeal can affect when possession may be enforced, but rent-registry and other Rule 510 requirements can matter.

writ_of_possession.label: WRIT OF POSSESSION
writ_of_possession.court: Texas Justice Court / executing constable or sheriff

immediate_clock.label: Writ issuance baseline
exceptions: perfected appeal and Rule 510 exceptions can change possession timing
immediate_clock.display: Rule 510.18 generally restricts issuance until the later of the sixth day after judgment or the day after the appeal deadline, subject to the rule and a perfected appeal.

execution.summary: Section 24.0061 governs execution of a writ, including the officer warning and removal process. Use the actual posted warning for the scheduled execution timing.
execution.local_practice_warning: Officer logistics can vary; do not infer one county's execution practice statewide.

do_now: Identify whether the writ is only requested, issued, or already posted for execution.
If an appeal was perfected, verify required rent-registry and appeal conditions immediately.
Save the writ/posting and contact eviction counsel if physical removal is imminent.

locked_out.label: LOCKED OUT
locked_out.court: Justice Court in the precinct where the rental premises are located
locked_out.required_filing: Sworn complaint requesting a writ of reentry under §92.009 when the statutory conditions are met.
locked_out.remedy: Justice Court writ of reentry for a qualifying unlawful residential lockout; the statute provides an expedited remedy rather than a generic damages-only route.
do_now: Document the lockout, time, notices, changed locks, landlord communications, and urgent access needs.
Do not assume every lock change qualifies; the remedy depends on a violation of the underlying lockout statute.

utility_shutoff.label: UTILITY SHUTOFF
utility_shutoff.court: Justice Court in the precinct where the rental premises are located
utility_shutoff.required_filing: Sworn complaint requesting a writ of restoration under §92.0091 when the statutory conditions are met.
utility_shutoff.remedy: Justice Court writ of restoration for a qualifying unlawful utility interruption by a residential landlord.
do_now: Document which utility was interrupted, when, by whom, all notices, account information, and landlord communications.
Do not assume every outage qualifies; the restoration remedy depends on an unlawful interruption under the underlying statute.

foreclosure_default_notice.label: NOTICE OF DEFAULT / INTENT TO ACCELERATE

immediate_clock.label: Residential cure period before notice of sale
exceptions: applies to a debtor in default under a deed of trust or other contract lien on real property used as the debtor's residence
loan documents and other law may create additional rights; acceleration doctrine is not reduced to this statutory cure period
immediate_clock.display: For covered residential contract-lien foreclosure, §51.002(d) gives at least 20 days to cure the default before notice of sale may be given.

do_now: Save the certified-mail notice and envelope; identify the mailing date, cure amount, servicer, loan number, property address, and any stated acceleration language.
Contact the servicer immediately about loss mitigation and, if the loan is VA-backed, contact VA Loan Guaranty assistance too.
If active-duty SCRA may apply, flag that separately; veteran status alone is not enough.

foreclosure_sale_notice.label: NOTICE OF FORECLOSURE SALE

immediate_clock.label: Notice before nonjudicial sale
exceptions: §51.002 contains exceptions and special provisions; loan type and other state/federal law may add requirements
immediate_clock.display: For an ordinary sale under §51.002(b), sale notice must generally be given at least 21 days before the sale date.

sale_baseline.summary: A covered nonjudicial sale is generally a public auction between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. on the first Tuesday of a month, at the statutorily authorized county location; the notice states the earliest sale time and the sale must begin at that time or within three hours after it.

do_now: Record the sale date, earliest sale time, county, servicer/trustee, and date the sale notice was mailed.

Request a current reinstatement/payoff or loss-mitigation status from the servicer if appropriate; do not assume §51.002 itself creates a universal reinstatement right beyond the verified cure notice.
Get foreclosure counsel immediately if the sale date is close, bankruptcy is being considered, or a complete loss-mitigation application is pending.

foreclosure_sale_completed.label: TRUSTEE SALE ALREADY HAPPENED
do_now: Save the trustee deed or sale information, all notices, loan history, and any post-sale demand for possession.
Do not assume the eviction/possession timeline from the mortgage sale itself; a later notice to vacate and possession suit can create a separate route.
Get Texas foreclosure/consumer counsel promptly to assess any challenge, redemption right that may exist for the specific foreclosure type, bankruptcy issue, or post-sale possession dispute.

home_equity_foreclosure_paper.label: HOME-EQUITY FORECLOSURE COURT PAPER
home_equity_foreclosure_paper.court: Texas district court or other court authorized by Rule 736
do_now: Do not treat this like an ordinary deed-of-trust sale notice. Texas home-equity and other liens listed in Rule 735 can require a Rule 736 court order or judicial foreclosure procedure.
Read the application, citation/order, cure history, and Texas constitutional/home-equity documents; obtain foreclosure counsel promptly.

hoa_poa_foreclosure_notice.label: HOA / POA FORECLOSURE NOTICE
hoa_poa_foreclosure_notice.court: Court involvement required for covered Texas POA assessment-lien foreclosure
do_now: Do not treat an HOA/POA assessment lien as an ordinary mortgage foreclosure.
Section 209.0092 generally requires a court order through expedited or judicial foreclosure procedures, subject to statutory exceptions and prerequisites.
Save all assessment notices, payment-plan communications, lien notices, court papers, and mortgage-lienholder notices.

tax_foreclosure_paper.label: TAX FORECLOSURE PAPER
do_now: Texas tax foreclosure uses a different statutory and judicial framework. No deadline is published in this pilot yet.
Save the petition, citation, judgment, tax statements, and sale notice and get tax-foreclosure/legal-aid help immediately.

va_home_loan_default.label: VA HOME LOAN DEFAULT LETTER
do_now: Contact the mortgage servicer first; a VA-backed loan is usually made and serviced by a private lender/servicer, with VA guaranteeing part of the loan rather than owning it.

Contact a VA loan technician at 877-827-3702. VA states that borrowers with VA-guaranteed loans may contact VA anytime and that VA automatically assigns a loan technician when a VA-guaranteed loan is 61 days past due.

Ask the servicer and VA about current foreclosure-avoidance options, which can include repayment plans, special forbearance, modifications, the current VA Partial Claim Program where eligible, short sale, or deed in lieu.

state_veterans_agency.note: TVC administers veteran-assistance grants that can include civil legal services. Provider scope varies.

state_bar_resources.name: Texas Lawyers for Texas Veterans
state_bar_resources.note: Clinic eligibility and subject coverage vary.

texaslawhelp.name: TexasLawHelp
texaslawhelp.note: Use court-specific instructions and current primary authority for deadlines.

lone_star_legal_aid.name: Lone Star Legal Aid
lone_star_legal_aid.note: Civil legal aid; eligibility and case acceptance vary by office and matter.

trla.name: Texas RioGrande Legal Aid
trla.note: Civil legal aid in listed central and southwest Texas counties; eligibility and case acceptance vary.

lsv_h.name: VA Legal Services for Veterans (LSV-H)
lsv_h.note: For eligible Veterans who are homeless or at risk; representation and subject coverage vary by grantee.

ssvf.name: Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF)
ssvf.note: Homelessness-prevention/rapid-rehousing services; not a statutory entitlement and availability varies.

local_rule_locator.name: Texas OCA Local Rules, Forms, and Standing Orders
local_rule_locator.note: Use the specific Justice Court/county before filing.

treatment_court_locator.name: Texas OCA Registered Specialty Courts
treatment_court_locator.note: Veterans Treatment Court availability and eligibility are county/program specific and do not replace criminal-defense counsel.

va_foreclosure_help.name: VA Home Loan foreclosure-avoidance help
va_foreclosure_help.note: VA-backed loans are generally serviced by private servicers; VA provides guaranty oversight and borrower assistance.

scra.warning: SCRA eviction and mortgage protections depend on covered military-service status, timing, and statutory conditions. Veteran status alone is insufficient.

fair_housing_act.warning: A disability-related reasonable-accommodation right can affect housing rules or procedures when legal requirements are met, but it is not an automatic defense to eviction or foreclosure.
